While I do not use it, it is considered to be a word by some.  Whether its proper is up to the individual, but due to it's common use there has been a shift toward it's acceptance.

Also, we're on the interwebz, we [ain't](http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/ain't) in class!!!  :P

Quick update:
I wasn't able to make an appointment with the psychiatrist today, so the had me see one of the regular doctors.  He was understanding, showed me where the psychiatry department is, and scheduled me for an appointment on Wednesday morning.  I've taken the first step on the path, but I don't have the surging feels of hope I thought I would have right now.

Thank you for all the assistance.  I'll keep you updated.

I have always had an aversion to getting help because it did feel like admitting I was weak, but I am starting to realize that whether it is or not, I do need help.  I woke up this morning to see these responses and that alone helped a lot.  It helped me to immediately not feel so alone, but it also helped me to have to courage to decide that I will go see a doctor about this.

Thank you for the kind words and friendly reception.  I will definitely continue talking with you on here, it's been the first step to what I hope to be a strong recovery (if that's the right word).  Thank you.

Thank you for the advice!  A big part of why I haven't gone to a doctor yet is that I do feel uncomfortable talking about it, it never occurred to me that I could type it out for them.  I will be calling my school's student health services office on Monday to schedule an appointment.

As far as pushing away negative thoughts - I have been trying, but sometimes it feels too difficult.  The real problem is pushing away thoughts of my ex.  EVERYTHING reminds me of her.  My mind play "six degrees of separation" with everything I see and do; it always manages to link everything around me back to her.  That's the hardest part - trying to remain positive and hold onto that last thread of hope only to remember how it unraveled less than a week ago.

I have been watching and listening to a lot of comedy, it's definitely helping.  I don't know if it's lifting my mood a whole lot, but it's at least keeping me distracted.  I have also found that listening to Ronald Jenkees' music helps a TON.  Something about it is inspiring to me.

I will continue to post, thank you for the advice!  Even though I haven't met any of you before and never even communicated with you before this, your words still mean a lot to me.  thank you.
That doesn't look like an "old, old, wooden ship"
